examples.scenario: DSM maximum is used as parcel terrain maximum.
examples.reason: DSM includes buildings, vehicles and vegetation; terrain semantics require DTM/bare-earth values.

examples.scenario: DTM and DSM filenames are similar and product type is inferred from suffix.
examples.reason: Terrain/surface semantics must come from authoritative product metadata, not filename guessing.

examples.scenario: A building roof creates the parcel maximum in a DSM.
examples.reason: Ground-terrain height must not include elevated man-made objects.

examples.scenario: Tree canopy produces the highest first-return elevation.
examples.reason: First-return DSM intentionally captures object tops as well as ground.

examples.scenario: Bare-earth class 2 points are mixed with water class 9 during terrain generation.
examples.reason: Water and ground classifications have distinct terrain semantics.

examples.scenario: Bridge-deck class 17 is retained in a bare-earth DEM.
examples.reason: USGS bare-earth DEM treatment removes bridge decks.

examples.scenario: Terrain beneath a bridge is linearly inferred but interpolation method is not recorded.
examples.reason: Below-bridge terrain is derived and must be auditable.

examples.scenario: Road over a culvert is removed as if it were a bridge.
examples.reason: Topographic bare-earth treatment preserves roads over culverts.

examples.scenario: Ignored-ground class 20 points near a breakline are included in DEM generation.
examples.reason: Such points may be excluded specifically to prevent interpolation artifacts.

examples.scenario: Water-surface elevation is reported with the same accuracy claim as land terrain.
examples.reason: USGS does not assert lidar water-surface elevation accuracy for topographic DEMs.

examples.scenario: Hydro-flattened DEM is described as hydrologically enforced.
examples.reason: Hydro-flattening is a topographic/cartographic treatment, not hydro-enforcement or hydro-conditioning.

examples.scenario: A flat lake surface is treated as directly measured lidar truth.
examples.reason: Flattened water can be breakline-driven derived treatment.

examples.scenario: Breaklines were used but not delivered or hashed.
examples.reason: Breaklines are part of the DEM-generation provenance.

examples.scenario: Breakline CRS differs from lidar CRS but geometries look aligned.
examples.reason: Visual similarity does not establish identical spatial reference.

examples.scenario: Breakline Z values change but raster extrema happen to match.
examples.reason: Equal output does not erase source-elevation provenance drift.

examples.scenario: Composite DTM uses a different contributing survey after an update.
examples.reason: Environment Agency composites may select newest/best-resolution surveys by location.

examples.scenario: Survey phase is ignored because the product name is unchanged.
examples.reason: Repeat survey phases encode temporally distinct source data.

examples.scenario: A 2022 composite is assumed to have a single acquisition date.
examples.reason: Composite products merge surveys collected across multiple dates/years.

examples.scenario: 10m DTM extrema are reported as native lidar extrema.
examples.reason: The 10m product is bilinearly resampled from 2m data.

examples.scenario: 1m composite cell was created by bilinear resampling but treated as direct laser return.
examples.reason: Composite cells may be derived by interpolation before merge.

examples.scenario: Two products have equal resolution but one is native and one resampled.
examples.reason: Cell size alone does not prove source-value identity.

examples.scenario: Higher-resolution Time Stamped DTM exists but a coarser composite is chosen silently.
examples.reason: Native available resolution and source lineage must be explicit.

examples.scenario: Historic DTM lacks matching archived point cloud and this is hidden.
examples.reason: Environment Agency notes historic rasters may not have matching point-cloud archives.

examples.scenario: Point cloud contains ground and surface-object classes but classification version is absent.
examples.reason: Raster terrain semantics depend on how returns were classified.

examples.scenario: A no-data hole is filled by interpolation before extrema computation.
examples.reason: Interpolated void values are derived, not native terrain measurements.

examples.scenario: NODATA is interpreted as numeric zero.
examples.reason: Void/no-data state must remain separate from valid elevation zero.

examples.scenario: Insufficient lidar coverage is treated as a flat region.
examples.reason: USGS treats qualifying coverage gaps as data voids and grounds for rejection.

examples.scenario: Right-edge raster tile has a gap to adjacent tile.
examples.reason: Tiled deliverables must edge-match seamlessly without gaps.

examples.scenario: Classification texture changes abruptly at a tile boundary.
examples.reason: USGS requires classification consistency across non-natural project divisions.

examples.scenario: Vertical RMSE metadata is used as guaranteed error for every raster cell.
examples.reason: Dataset-level accuracy reporting is not a per-cell deterministic error bound.

examples.scenario: Slope raster maximum is substituted for terrain elevation maximum.
examples.reason: Slope is a derived neighborhood metric with different units.

examples.scenario: Aspect raster values are considered elevation candidates.
examples.reason: Aspect is a derived azimuth, not height.

examples.scenario: Hillshade brightness is used to infer terrain extrema.
examples.reason: Hillshade is visualization derived from terrain and illumination parameters.

examples.scenario: TRI/TPI/roughness outputs replace source DTM values.
examples.reason: Terrain morphology derivatives are not base elevations.

examples.scenario: Slope edge interpolation creates values near NODATA and these are reported as terrain elevations.
examples.reason: Derivative interpolation does not create authoritative DTM cells.

examples.scenario: A DTM cell represents a 1m area but is described as an exact surveyed point at the cell center.
examples.reason: Raster cells represent an area/sample support and need not equal an original lidar return.

examples.scenario: PixelIsArea flag is missing on a bare-earth raster and ignored.
examples.reason: USGS bare-earth DEM delivery requires PixelIsArea.

examples.scenario: Perennial snow is present but classification policy is unknown.
examples.reason: Current USGS specification explicitly versions snow classification/treatment.

examples.scenario: Primary replay uses composite DTM while independent replay uses Time Stamped DTM.
examples.reason: Different terrain products can legitimately contain different values.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent DTM bytes match but survey-lineage metadata differs.
examples.reason: Byte equality alone does not prove identical documented source provenance.

examples.scenario: Survey-lineage metadata matches but DTM bytes differ.
examples.reason: Same provenance label does not permit different runtime raster content.

examples.scenario: Composite feathering at survey overlap is ignored.
examples.reason: Overlap blending can create derived values distinct from either source survey.

examples.scenario: Dataset says +/-15cm RMSE and code rounds all elevations to 0.15m.
examples.reason: Accuracy metadata is not a storage resolution or rounding instruction.

examples.scenario: Static DTM semantic QA passes and a target parcel elevation is emitted.
examples.reason: No canonical target sampling has executed.

examples.scenario: A fixture parcel proves ground filtering and its numbers are copied to production.
examples.reason: Examples validate logic only.

examples.scenario: Known ACK blocker is relabelled pending.
examples.reason: Known unresolved execution conditions remain BLOCKED; pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: A second terrain runner is launched while ACK is absent.
examples.reason: Continuation contract requires the existing shared runner only.

examples.scenario: 99.99 source readiness is published as vertical accuracy.
examples.reason: Preparation readiness is not measured terrain accuracy.

examples.scenario: Water, bridge and resampled cells are all accepted into one extrema pool without provenance flags.
examples.reason: Cell origin/treatment must be known before terminal extrema selection.

examples.scenario: Batch 82 is reported as final parcel height-difference output.
examples.reason: Canonical point, exact boundary, immutable DTM runtime binding and executed sampling are still required.
